purpose: Bounded Linux trial of covered unit tests with selective process isolation and Nx Core task caching; this is historical evidence, not an adopted gate
machine: local Linux host; /usr/bin/time process-tree user+system CPU and elapsed wall seconds

commands.directTuned: npm run build; node --import tsx tools/nx-evaluation/tuned-unit-runner.ts safe; node --import tsx tools/nx-evaluation/tuned-unit-runner.ts unsafe

candidate.sameInput: 6f31f888b / 62187a2a5 trial revisions; identical clean candidate in a second worktree restored build and both LCOV outputs byte-for-byte without execution markers
candidate.changedInput: cbd64e27a in second worktree changes only a comment in src/domain/comparators.ts; all three conservatively hashed targets reran

coverage.comparison: Both LCOV reports passed through the repository coverage-merge normalization before comparing source/line covered sets
coverage.result: All assertions passed in both modes, but the covered-line sets differ; the shared-process selection was not proven semantically equivalent

pluginInvestigation.finding: The package exports a node:test executor with a testFiles glob; it declares no Nx createNodes/createDependencies plugin and does not infer transitive affected tests or preserve the repository's guarded runner
pluginInvestigation.alternativeCost: Official Jest/Vitest Atomizer support requires migrating the test runner, and file splitting alone does not establish per-test-file source dependencies

dependencyAudit: Nx 23.2.1 introduced two high npm audit findings via its pinned smol-toml 1.6.1 on the trial date; see ignored raw audit output. Trial wiring was removed instead of weakening the mandatory audit gate.
